description: Guide a student to implement a pairs trading strategy on LEAN that (1) uses a pre-computed candidate pairs file (I05_candidate_pairs.json) listing top-10 correlated pairs selected from the full 635-symbol Tier 2 universe using only pre-backtest data, (2) implements spread mean-reversion trading on the selected pairs with z-score entry/exit rules, and (3) manages multi-leg positions with proper exposure caps. The student should understand pair selection concepts but does not need to compute pairwise statistics from scratch. This is how institutional stat-arb strategies work — the pair discovery phase is provided in a point-in-time-safe form so the task focuses on implementation of spread trading and multi-pair portfolio management without look-ahead bias.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I have price data for a big crypto futures universe and a file of pre-computed candidate pairs. How do I trade those pairs automatically on LEAN without introducing look-ahead bias?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I need to implement a pairs trading strategy on LEAN using a PIT-safe candidate-pairs file generated from the full 635-symbol universe, then trade spread mean-reversion. How do I structure the pair loading and multi-leg position management?
student_openings.advanced_quant: I'm implementing a cross-asset stat-arb strategy on LEAN using precomputed PIT-safe candidate pairs drawn from the full crypto futures universe. What's the best architecture for pairs-based trading?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Student produces a LEAN C# algorithm that (1) loads candidate pairs from I05_candidate_pairs.json, (2) subscribes to the relevant symbols, (3) tracks per-pair ratio z-scores, (4) enters/exits spread positions atomically per pair, (5) manages portfolio exposure across up to 10 active pairs, and (6) produces per-pair trade logs and a portfolio-level summary. Trade logs for 3 reference pairs should match the ground-truth.
required_capabilities: Load and parse pre-computed candidate pairs from I05_candidate_pairs.json
Subscribe to symbols from the candidate pairs and understand that pair selection was done point-in-time using only pre-backtest data
Manage multiple simultaneous spread positions (up to 10 pairs × 2 legs = 20 positions)
Implement atomic spread entry/exit with per-pair stop-loss
